purpose: Bounded Fair Work Commission and court-enforcement case preserving partial compensation payment, residual unpaid loss, enforcement, and penalty as separate remedy stages.

events.geography: Australia; Fair Work Division of the Federal Circuit Court, Fair Work Commission enforcement example
events.date_precision: court judgment date; Commission compensation order ran from September 2018 through February 2019
events.denominator: One publicly summarized adjudicated enforcement case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Commission enforcement page
events.missingness: Worker identity beyond the public case, original dismissal circumstances, alternatives, household effects, payment instrument, later employment, trust, recurrence, and exit are not retained; payment amounts are reported by the institution rather than independently audited here
events.exposure: The worker was found unfairly dismissed and the Commission ordered $18,000 compensation, payable in six instalments from September 2018 through February 2019
events.alternatives_before_action: The public enforcement summary does not report substitute employment, non-use, bargaining alternatives, or household buffers
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The employer did not make the ordered instalments as required; at the enforcement application only $5,000 had been paid, and later payments brought the total to $7,000 while $5,008 remained outstanding after tax
events.choice_or_response: The Fair Work Ombudsman applied to the Court in March 2019 to enforce the order; the employer's financial difficulty and cooperation were considered in the enforcement outcome
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer controlled instalment execution; the worker bore the consequences of delay; the Fair Work Ombudsman and Court controlled enforcement and penalty routes
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Court ordered payment of the outstanding $5,008 plus interest and imposed a $5,000 fine, after the employer had made only partial payments
events.remedy_receipt: The official summary reports $7,000 paid against the order and $5,008 outstanding after tax at the enforcement stage; later receipt is not observed
events.durability_followup: The record ends at partial payment, enforcement, and penalty; later work, household recovery, recurrence, trust, switching, and exit are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Partial compensation implementation and a residual unpaid balance are reported, followed by court enforcement and a further payment order
events.protected_outcome: Some monetary compensation was delivered and the enforcement route preserved a claim to the remaining amount; restored employment and durable livelihood are not verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Payment delay and the outstanding balance left the worker exposed to residual income loss and enforcement delay; later household effects are unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The worker and public enforcement system carried delay and enforcement effort while employer financial difficulty affected payment timing; the Court transferred a further legal obligation and penalty to the employer
events.later_outcome: The institution reports partial payment, an outstanding balance, and a subsequent order for the balance plus interest; no later lived recovery endpoint is public
events.meaning_and_attribution: The enforcement record attributes the unresolved balance to noncompliance and financial difficulty; it contains no worker-reported trust or meaning measure
events.public_or_collective_response: Public enforcement by the Fair Work Ombudsman is observed; no later collective action or political response is reported
events.counterexample: A compensation order can produce real partial payment while leaving a material balance unpaid and employment restoration unaddressed
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Fair Work Commission enforcement page, https://www.fwc.gov.au/role-court-unfair-dismissal-cases; it reports the order, payment totals, outstanding balance, employer financial difficulty, further order, and fine, but is not a payment-instrument audit or claimant follow-up

arrows.from: Commission compensation order with scheduled instalments
arrows.evidence: The official summary reports $5,000 paid at the enforcement application, $7,000 paid after the Court's April orders, and $5,008 still outstanding after tax
arrows.counterexample: A scheduled payment plan and some payment do not establish full or timely receipt
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment instrument, exact timing, worker confirmation, and final receipt

arrows.evidence: The Fair Work Ombudsman applied to the Court in March 2019 after the ordered instalments were not made as required
arrows.counterexample: Enforcement access is visible in this institutional record but is not evidence that every affected worker can use it
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker effort, delay cost, representation, and alternative enforcement routes

arrows.to: further balance order, interest, and fine
arrows.evidence: The official page reports an order for the outstanding $5,008 plus interest and a $5,000 fine
arrows.counterexample: A further order and penalty do not establish final payment or livelihood recovery
arrows.remaining_gap: Post-judgment payment, net receipt, later employment, and household outcome

arrows.to: durable recovery, trust, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The official institutional record ends at partial payment, outstanding balance, further order, and fine
arrows.counterexample: Enforcement can improve monetary remedy while leaving employment access, later security, and trust unobserved
arrows.remaining_gap: Final receipt, later work, household recovery, trust, recurrence, collective action, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger adds an official partial-payment enforcement endpoint. It demonstrates that reported receipt can be incomplete and delayed, without establishing final payment, restored employment, adequate recovery, or general prevalence.
storage_boundary: No claimant file, payment instrument, direct personal data beyond the public case reference, or bulk archive is retained; only bounded institutional summary fields, remedy sequence, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.
